outlook.statement: The underlying objective of the rationalisation programme has been to move away from carrying capacity in anticipation of volume and to align the Company's manufacturing platform more closely with the level and nature of business available.

Management's priority remains the restoration of sustainable profitability, while retaining the capabilities and customer relationships required to participate in future growth opportunities. The Company will continue to evaluate opportunities for expansion as the business environment improves while maintaining discipline over capacity, costs and working-capital deployment.

Changes in global trade arrangements and the continued development of free trade agreements may improve India's competitiveness in certain markets and product categories, providing an opportunity for the Company to pursue new markets while broadening the product portfolio offered to established customers.

The company has implemented various initiatives to improve on the efficiencies and control the losses. In view of the various strategic initiatives that the Company is exploring, it is confident of being able to continue and operate the business on a "Going Concern" basis.

risks: Replacing volume alone would not be sufficient; a larger and more fragmented portfolio, particularly where programmes were highly price-sensitive, increased operating complexity without necessarily generating the contribution required to support the Company's existing manufacturing and fixed-cost structure.
